topStories.headline: Alma Fire Burns 653 Acres Southeast of Ennis, Fully Contained After FM 85 Evacuations
topStories.dek: A fast-moving grass fire ignited September 4 near the community of Alma, forcing residents along FM 85 to evacuate before crews brought it fully under control the following day.
topStories.body:
A brush fire that ignited during the afternoon of Friday, September 4, 2026, southeast of Ennis quickly grew to 653 acres before emergency crews gained control. The blaze, officially named the Alma Fire by the Texas A&M Forest Service, forced evacuations for residents from Zmolek Road to Bruce Road along FM 85 as it moved north from FM 1182 east of Alma. Emergency road closures were placed on FM 1182, FM 85, Walker Creek Road, Mach Road, and Zmolek Road.

The City of Ennis assisted Ellis County with evacuations, and an evacuation center was established at Cowboy Church of Ennis, 7450 S. Interstate 45 Service Road. By approximately 8:40 p.m. on September 4, with the fire at 600 acres and 20 percent contained, the evacuation notice was lifted and residents were told they could safely return home. Ellis County Precinct 2 officials deployed water trucks and heavy equipment alongside local fire departments and Texas A&M Forest Service crews.

By the morning of September 5, fire tracking data listed the Alma Fire at 653 acres and 100 percent contained. The fire burned entirely on private land in Ellis County. It ignited under the active county-wide burn ban that the Ellis County Commissioners' Court had enacted on July 21, 2026, prohibiting all open outdoor burning in unincorporated parts of the county. The cause of the fire remained under investigation as of the last official update on September 5.

topStories.headline: Yellowstone Spinoff 'The Dutton Ranch' Has Been Filming in Ferris Since Mid-August
topStories.dek: Paramount selected Ferris as a primary shooting location for a new Yellowstone spinoff featuring Beth Dutton and Rip Wheeler, bringing national attention and local casting calls to the small North Texas city.
topStories.body:
The city of Ferris announced in August 2025 that Paramount Pictures had selected it as a primary filming location for a new Yellowstone spinoff series, initially known by the working title 'Rio Palo' and later confirmed as 'The Dutton Ranch.' The show stars Kelly Reilly and Cole Hauser, who reprise their Yellowstone roles as Beth Dutton and Rip Wheeler respectively, and is expected to be a multi-season Paramount+ production. Finn Little, who played their adopted son Carter on the original series, also joins the cast.

Filming has taken place at various locations around Ferris and across the wider North Texas region, including Cleburne, Weatherford, Rio Vista, Fort Worth, and Mineral Wells, according to casting notices from Texas-based Legacy Casting. The production continued casting local extras for roles including concession stand workers, rodeo attendees, and restaurant patrons. City Manager Brooks Williams stated that the decision affirms Ferris as a community with roots that can still move forward, and that city officials are proud to show what Ferris has to offer.

Ferris, a city of roughly 4,000 people located about 20 miles south of downtown Dallas along I-45 in Dallas and Ellis counties, is historically known for the Ferris Brick Company, whose bricks appear in streets, schools, and courthouses across the country. City officials said a specific Ferris site will serve as the central home of the show's lead characters, though the exact location has not been publicly identified. No premiere date for the series has been announced by Paramount.

topStories.headline: Ennis City Commission Posts Special Meeting for September 29
topStories.dek: The Ennis City Commission has scheduled a special session for Monday, September 29, capping a month that also included a special meeting on September 8 and an Economic Development Corporation board meeting on September 24.
topStories.body:
The Ennis City Commission has scheduled a Special Meeting for Monday, September 29, 2026. The agenda — a 212-kilobyte PDF — has been posted to the city's official website at ennistx.gov for public review in advance of the session. The meeting follows a busy September that included a City Commission Special Meeting on September 8 and an Economic Development Corporation Board meeting on September 24.

Regular City Commission sessions are held the first and third Tuesday of each month at 6:00 p.m. in the Commission Chambers at Ennis City Hall, 107 N. Sherman St. The Commission-Manager form of government, which Ennis has operated under since 1957, gives the Commission responsibility for adopting the city budget, passing ordinances, appointing committees, and hiring the City Manager, City Secretary, City Attorney, and Municipal Judge. Residents who wish to address commissioners on matters not listed on the September 29 agenda may submit a Public Comment Period card to the City Secretary before the meeting begins.

moreNews.headline: Ellis County Burn Ban Remains in Effect
moreNews.body: The Ellis County Commissioners' Court voted to place a county-wide burn ban effective immediately at their meeting on Tuesday, July 21, 2026. The ban covers all unincorporated areas of Ellis County and was listed as active on the county's official website as of this week. The Alma Fire, which burned 653 acres near Ennis on September 4–5, ignited while the ban was already in force. Residents should check elliscountytx.gov for the current status before any outdoor burning.

moreNews.headline: Palmer ISD Board Adopts $1.0063 Tax Rate for 2026–27
moreNews.body: The Palmer Independent School District Board of Trustees voted unanimously 7–0 at its August 19, 2026 regular meeting to adopt a property tax rate of $1.0063 per $100 valuation for the 2026–27 school year, split into $0.71130 per $100 for maintenance and operations and $0.29500 per $100 for interest and sinking. The district's website notes the adopted rate will raise more taxes for maintenance and operations than last year's rate of $1.05020, in part because rising property valuations increase revenue. The board also unanimously approved the final amended 2025–26 budget and the new 2026–27 budget at the same meeting.

moreNews.headline: City of Ennis Purchasing Division Wins National Procurement Award
moreNews.body: The City of Ennis announced that its Purchasing Division has been awarded the 2026 Achievement of Excellence in Procurement (AEP), a national honor from the National Procurement Institute recognizing outstanding performance in professional, ethical, and transparent procurement practices. The award program, established in 1995, evaluated 269 applications from 28 states and Canada this year; 251 organizations earned the designation. The Ennis division is led by Katrinia Roberson. City Manager Andrea Weckmueller-Behringer credited the division's dedication and professionalism, noting the award reflects the city's commitment to responsible stewardship of public funds.
